From: Priya Shah <pshah@finly.com>

Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing for function-calls + JSON output (rate card request)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this — we're evaluating Redwood's hosted API for a new payments reconciliation feature and need some concrete numbers to show procurement. A few specifics so you can tailor the rate card:

- Estimated monthly model tokens (generated + prompt): ~15,000,000 tokens.
- Estimated function/tool invocations: ~300,000 calls/month. Each call includes a ~1KB JSON payload (tool args) and we expect the model to return structured JSON (JSON mode / function-calling).
- Typical request sizes: prompt ~150 tokens, expected model output ~200 tokens; function call payloads vary but average ~250 tokens when serialized.
- Peak concurrency: ~40 TPS sustained bursts to 120 TPS for short windows.

Questions:
1) How are function/tool calls metered? Are they just token-based (prompt + generated) or is there an additional per-call charge when you run hosted tool integrations/webhook routing?
2) Does using JSON mode/structured output (validated schema) change token metering or introduce per-response processing fees?
3) Do you have baseline hosted API rate cards and committed-spend discount tiers (12-month)? We want example math for our 15M tokens + 300k calls to share with procurement.

Can you send a rate card PDF and a sample cost calc? We may be able to commit to a 12-month term if the economics look right.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Sr. Product Manager — Data Platform
Finly, Inc.
Attachment: sample_usage_breakdown.xlsx (CSV stub)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing for function-calls + JSON output (rate card request)

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear breakdown. I'm attaching our current public rate card to start (see rate_card_v1.pdf) and sketched a few clarifying points below — will follow up with a worked example once I have peak token-per-request ceilings and concurrency confirmation.

Key notes up front:
- Metering: For hosted API the model usage is primarily token-based: prompt tokens + model output tokens are billed per the rate card.
- Function/tool calling: If you use Redwood's function-calling feature where the model returns a JSON payload and Redwood routes an integration (webhook) to execute tools, you are billed for the model tokens as above plus a small per-execution hosted-integration fee (we charge $0.0005 per hosted webhook execution to cover routing/egress costs).
- JSON mode/structured output: Enabling structured output (JSON mode or function calling) does not change the per-token rate. Validation or lightweight schema enforcement on the control plane is included. Heavy post-processing (e.g., server-side schema transformation) may be subject to an additional managed-processing fee, but that only applies when Redwood is asked to run custom transformation pipelines.

Quick example (ballpark):
- Base generation rate (hosted, non-committed): $0.004 per 1k tokens.
- Per-hosted-integration execution fee: $0.0005 per execution.

If your 15M tokens/month are at $0.004 / 1k tokens -> 15,000 * $0.004 = $60.00 (note: that's an illustrative per-1k math; we'll provide exact cents). The function call executions at 300k * $0.0005 = $150.

I'll prepare a worked estimate for: (a) standard hosted with no commit, (b) 12-mo commit tiers (10% off at $10k/mo, 18% off at $30k/mo), and (c) a dedicated/reserved capacity option if your latency SLOs demand it.

Questions for you to finalize the calc:
- Are your function calls using Redwood-hosted webhooks (we would route to your endpoints), or are you returning a function call payload to be executed in your environment? The former triggers the per-exec fee above; the latter does not.
- Any max tokens-per-request cap we should assume? (helps size concurrency and queueing).
- Do you care about streaming? Streaming affects tail latency and connection management but not token metering.

Attached: rate_card_v1.pdf (public), sample_prompt_set.json (small sample of representative prompts).

If it helps I can schedule a 30-minute pricing workshop with our Solutions Engineering team and bring a simple spreadsheet calc.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: rate_card_v1.pdf (PDF stub); sample_prompt_set.json (JSON stub)
From: Priya Shah <pshah@finly.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing for function-calls + JSON output (rate card request)

Rafael — thanks, that's helpful. A few answers and clarifications:

- We'll likely use function calling where the model returns a JSON payload and our service executes the action (so Redwood would not need to run our webhooks in the hosted path). That should mean no hosted-exec fee, correct?
- Max tokens per request: plan for up to 1,200 tokens total (prompt + output + serialized tool args).
- Distribution: 65% of requests will be plain generation (no tool call), 35% will involve function-calling.
- Streaming: yes, we want streaming for UX but agree it's not a metering difference.
- Procurement asks: a two-tier committed-spend discount makes more sense for our procurement process (Tier A = $10k/mo commit, Tier B = $25k/mo). We may be able to commit to Tier B for 12 months if your math supports it.

Also, curious about how structured output 'schema validation' is handled in practice — does Redwood run post-processing on the response to enforce strict JSON (and is that ever charged)? We prefer any validation to be client-side.

Can you send a worked pricing sheet with Tier A / Tier B numbers and a clear call-out of what triggers per-exec fees (if any)? We'll need that for our SOW.

Thanks,
Priya

Priya — thanks for the answers. Below is a worked example using your numbers and two committed tiers we typically offer. I've attached a short proposal and a spreadsheet-style calc in the PDF so you can paste numbers into procurement docs.

Assumptions used:
- Total model tokens / month: 15,000,000 (prompt + model output + serialized tool args).
- Function-calls: 300,000 (35% of traffic). We assume your execution is client-side (no hosted webhook routing), so no per-hosted-exec fee applies.
- Base hosted list rate: $0.004 / 1k tokens.
- Tier A (commit $10k/mo): 10% off token rate.
- Tier B (commit $25k/mo): 20% off token rate for first year.

Calculations (rounded):
1) No-commit (list): 15,000k tokens -> 15,000 * $0.004 = $60.00 (monthly model token cost at list rates).
   - Function-calls do not add extra model token charges beyond tokens included above. No per-exec fee since you run execution client-side.
2) Tier A (10% off): effective rate $0.0036 / 1k -> 15,000 * $0.0036 = $54.00/month (committed pricing).
3) Tier B (20% off): effective rate $0.0032 / 1k -> 15,000 * $0.0032 = $48.00/month.

Notes and clarifications:
- The numbers above illustrate token-cost math using 1k-block pricing for easy procurement. Our actual invoices break down prompt vs completion tokens and will carry cents-level precision.
- If you start using Redwood-hosted integrations (we route a webhook to your service from our control plane) we would separately bill $0.0005 per hosted-exec to cover egress and monitoring; this is not applied when you execute the returned function call in your infra.
- Structured JSON mode: we do lightweight schema validation for correctness (well-formed JSON + schema shape) as part of the response pipeline; that validation is included with hosted API and is not billed separately. Heavy managed transformations (e.g., mapping to internal canonical objects with retries and DLQ) are an add-on and would be scoped.
- Concurrency: your peak 120 TPS burst can be handled on hosted with reasonable throttling. If you require strict guaranteed p99 latency under bursts we can discuss Dedicated capacity estimates (reserved GPU).

Attachments: proposal_draft.pdf (worked numbers + legal bullets), sample_prompt_set.json (example prompts and token estimates).

Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 30-minute pricing workshop with Solutions Engineering and one of our platform engineers to validate token calculations and concurrency headroom.
- If procurement wants a SOW with a Tier B 12-month commitment, I can draft a simple addendum with the agreed discount and termination terms.

Can you confirm whether we should schedule the workshop next Tuesday or Thursday?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
